open_questions: Duration ratio 1.533 (observed 1.246h vs central 0.8129h) and star_density_penalty 5407 with fit_log_density_ratio -2.416 indicate transit is much longer than central for TIC density; slope likely from large spot modulation (rotation period 1.018 d = signal period 1.01752 d, amplitudes 19173-27962 ppm); duration/density to refine with RV/companion density solution.
dossier.public_summary: A 1.02-day flat-bottomed 4583 ppm dip repeats 87 times on the 30 pc M-dwarf and sits on target with no secondary or odd-even change. Spot variability at the same period makes the out-of-transit light curve vary strongly and makes the transit look long, but the dip depth and flat shape match a ~2 Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Flat-bottomed dip favours planet over V-shaped grazing binary on target; best_ingress_fraction 0.1 and fit_b 0.5212 consistent with transit.
No secondary at any phase (snr_at_half -25.22, depth -18 ppm) argues against EB on target; phase_curve ratio 1.386 and chi2 1652 are from spots.
Odd/even depths 4225 ppm vs 4433 ppm consistent (difference 208.4 ppm), no sign of period doubled binary.
Difference imaging in 4 sectors centers on target (offset 1.786 arcsec err 1.71 arcsec sigma 1.045) and all three suspects ruled out >42 sigma, neighbours.plausible_within_1px 0.
Undiluted depth 4598 ppm on M-dwarf (TIC rad 0.2824, Teff 3249 K) gives 2.09 Rearth planet; similar candidates all confirmed planets.

sectors p_constant 0.001461 looks significant, but tool shows p_constant within each pipeline 0.296 and 0.297 is steady; only TESS-SPOC vs SPOC 2-min calibration difference (3802 vs 4987 ppm), not astrophysical change.
